title: Donald Trump calls Venezuela a US 'new acquisition'
summary: United States President Donald Trump on Wednesday described Venezuela as the country's "new acquisition," drawing attention to Washington's control over the South American nation's energy resources.

blocks.text: United States President Donald Trump on Wednesday described Venezuela as the country's "new acquisition," drawing attention to Washington's control over the South American nation's energy resources.
"Venezuela, which was our new acquisition," Trump said during a speech ahead of his bilateral talks with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at Malacañang.
"It was an acquisition, whether people like to say that or not. And it's been amazing what's happened to the United States," he added.
Trump made the remarks while discussing the United States' energy supply, making the country supposedly the world's leading producer of oil and natural gas "by a lot."
"We have more energy than any country in the world by double, even more than that. If you add Russia and Saudi Arabia together, we're much bigger than those two combined," he said.
"And then you add Venezuela, which was our new acquisition. It was an acquisition whether people like to say that or not. And it's been amazing what happened to the United States," Trump added.

Trump said the United States was looking to expand its energy exports to allies in the Pacific, including the Philippines, citing a planned major pipeline project in Alaska and the country's vast oil and natural gas reserves.
In January, US forces attacked Venezuela and ousted its longtime President, Nicolás Maduro.
Following what he described as a "successful" overnight military operation, Trump said US forces would remain in Venezuela until a new government was established.

Venezuela has millions of barrels of oil loaded on tankers and stored in storage facilities that it has been unable to ship because of a US blockade on its oil exports imposed by Trump in mid-December 2025.
The blockade was part of Washington's escalating pressure campaign against the Maduro government.
Trump arrived at Malacañang on Wednesday for his state visit to the Philippines.
During his meeting with Marcos, Trump announced that the two countries had secured a "big" trade deal but did not provide further details.
Philippine Ambassador to the United States Jose Manuel Romualdez, meanwhile, said the agreement involved food and energy supplies.
"The US offered for us to diversify our food supply and energy requirements," he said.— MCG, GMA News
